title: Stop a hand texture test when the feel is unclear
description: Work through the feel only as far as you can answer, and say the test is not a lab result.
oneStarDescription: Say whether the moist sample is mostly rough and gritty.
twoStarDescription: When you cannot tell sticky from silky, stop and write 'unclear'.
threeStarDescription: Say that a percentage, or a map class, would need a lab or a soil map, not this pinch.

title: Tell a sticky soil from a gritty one
description: Wet two samples and say which sticks to your fingers more. Clay sticks more than sand.
oneStarDescription: Add a little water to two labelled samples.
twoStarDescription: Rub each between finger and thumb.
threeStarDescription: Say which one sticks more, and call that the clayier sample. Wash your hands.

title: Tune to a reference as the last check
description: Before you play with a piano or another fixed pitch, make the last tuning check against that pitch.
oneStarDescription: Tune as far as you can before you enter.
twoStarDescription: Play the reference note and bring your note to it.
threeStarDescription: If you cannot tune it, say so and wait for help rather than starting the piece out of tune.

title: Warm up before someone is ready to listen
description: If the listening room is close, warm the fingers or the voice quietly, then play a few notes once you are in the room.
oneStarDescription: Arrive early enough to get the music out and settle.
twoStarDescription: If people can hear the performance room, warm up without playing aloud, or use a room set aside for it.
threeStarDescription: Once it is your turn, play or sing a few notes before the piece.

title: Baste two layers with stitches you can pull out
description: Hold two scraps with long temporary stitches, then take the thread out.
oneStarDescription: Pin two scraps and sew a few long stitches that are easy to see.
twoStarDescription: Hold the layers and tug once. The stitches should still hold them.
threeStarDescription: Draw the thread out and separate the layers.

title: Bring in the next voice of a round
description: Cue a second group to start at the next phrase, quietly enough that both groups can hear each other.
oneStarDescription: Agree which phrase is the moment the second voice starts.
twoStarDescription: Cue the second group at that phrase while the first group continues.
threeStarDescription: Keep both parts quiet enough that each group can hear the other. If it falls apart, stop and return to unison.

title: Capture a pawn en passant
description: On the move just after a pawn advances two squares, capture it as if it had moved only one.
oneStarDescription: Set a pawn that has just moved two squares beside an opposing pawn that can capture it.
twoStarDescription: Move the capturing pawn to the square the other pawn passed, and remove the captured pawn.
threeStarDescription: Say that this capture is legal only on that next move, and do not play it a move later.

title: End a round one group at a time
description: Cue one group to stop at the end of its line, then let the other group finish its own line.
oneStarDescription: While the round is going, point to the group that will stop at the end of its line.
twoStarDescription: Cue that group to stop, and let the other group keep going to the end of its line.
threeStarDescription: Wait until both groups are silent, and say which group stopped first.

title: Fill a small shape with satin stitch
description: Lay straight stitches side by side, all in one direction, until a small shape reads as a solid patch.
oneStarDescription: Place two straight stitches next to each other, parallel and touching.
twoStarDescription: Fill one half of a small shape with stitches that stay parallel.
threeStarDescription: Fill the other half. The shape should read as a solid patch, not as scattered lines.

title: Move the piece you touched
description: On a practice board, if you touch your own piece, move that piece if it has a legal move.
oneStarDescription: Touch one of your pieces that has a legal move.
twoStarDescription: Move the piece you touched, not a different one.
threeStarDescription: If you had touched an opponent's piece instead, say that you would have to capture it when that capture is legal.

title: Offer a draw before you press the clock
description: Make the move, offer the draw, and only then press the clock. Wait for an answer.
oneStarDescription: Make a legal move on the board.
twoStarDescription: Say that you offer a draw before you press your clock.
threeStarDescription: Do not play another move until the other person has accepted or refused.

title: Say why castling is stopped
description: Point to the reason a castle cannot be played: a moved king or rook, a piece in the way, or the king moving through an attacked square.
oneStarDescription: Point to a king and rook that have not moved, with empty squares between them.
twoStarDescription: Point to one block: a piece between them, or the king's square, the square it crosses, or the square it would land on being attacked.
threeStarDescription: Do not play the castle, and say which reason you found.

title: Sew a back stitch with no gaps
description: Work each surface stitch backward into the end of the one before, so the line is solid.
oneStarDescription: Come up a stitch-length along the line and go down at the start.
twoStarDescription: Come up ahead and go down into the end of the previous stitch.
threeStarDescription: Show a short line whose surface stitches touch, with no gap between them.

title: Sew a chain of loops
description: Make interlocking loops, each held by the next, and finish the last loop with a small stitch.
oneStarDescription: Come up and go down in the same place, leaving a loop on the surface.
twoStarDescription: Come up inside that loop and pull the loop snug against the needle.
threeStarDescription: Make a second loop the same way, then secure the last loop with a small holding stitch.

title: Sew a herringbone band
description: Cross diagonal stitches between two lines so they pass near each other's ends.
oneStarDescription: Draw two parallel lines and sew one diagonal from the lower line to the upper line.
twoStarDescription: Come up a little behind that point and sew a diagonal that crosses the first near its end.
threeStarDescription: Add more diagonals until you have a short band of crossed stitches.

title: Sew a stem stitch that twists
description: Come up beside the previous stitch, always on the same side, so a short line looks like a cord.
oneStarDescription: Make one straight stitch, then come up about halfway along it, to one side.
twoStarDescription: Keep the thread on that same side of the needle for the next stitch.
threeStarDescription: Finish a short line in which each stitch begins about halfway along the one before.

title: Sew an even running stitch
description: Make a line of straight stitches with gaps of about the same length, including on the underside.
oneStarDescription: Make the first stitch, then leave a gap about as long as that stitch.
twoStarDescription: Continue along a short line so the stitches you see match each other.
threeStarDescription: Turn the cloth and show that the stitches underneath are evenly spaced too.

title: Sew one detached chain
description: Make a single loop and hold it with a small stitch, without starting a second loop.
oneStarDescription: Come up, go down in the same place, and keep a loop on the surface.
twoStarDescription: Come up inside the loop and draw it snug against the needle.
threeStarDescription: Take a small stitch over the end of the loop. It stays, and you do not start another loop.

title: Sew one fly stitch
description: Pull a straight stitch into a V with a stitch that anchors the loop.
oneStarDescription: Take the needle up and down a short distance apart, leaving a loop.
twoStarDescription: Come up inside the loop so the thread pulls the stitch into a V.
threeStarDescription: Take the needle down just beyond the V so a small stitch holds it when you let go.

title: Sing a tune in unison before a round
description: Sing a short tune together, without a leader feeding the notes, before anyone starts late.
oneStarDescription: Sing or speak a short tune all the way through as one group.
twoStarDescription: Sing it again while nobody mouths the notes ahead of the group.
threeStarDescription: If the tune falls apart, stay in unison. Do not split into a round yet.

title: Split the thread of the previous stitch
description: Bring the needle up through the middle of the stitch you just made, so the line looks like a fine chain.
oneStarDescription: Sew one straight stitch on the line and pull the thread through.
twoStarDescription: Bring the needle up through the middle of that stitch so the thread splits.
threeStarDescription: Make the next stitch the same way, so each stitch is split by the one that follows.

title: Write one chess move in algebraic notation
description: Write one move with the square names so another person can play it.
oneStarDescription: Point to the square a piece leaves and the square it lands on, using the file letter and the rank number.
twoStarDescription: Write the landing square, and a letter for the piece when it is not a pawn.
threeStarDescription: Give the note to another person and have them play that one move.

title: Add the map legend's magnetic variation
description: After a bearing is set to grid north, rotate the housing by the variation printed in that map's legend.
oneStarDescription: Find the magnetic variation note in the legend of the map you are using.
twoStarDescription: With the baseplate still, rotate the housing by that amount in the direction the legend states.
threeStarDescription: Say you will not turn the housing again while you follow the arrow.

title: Move metal away before you read a compass
description: Put a phone, keys, or a knife aside, then see which end of the needle points north.
oneStarDescription: Put the phone and any knife or keys away from the compass.
twoStarDescription: Hold the compass flat, away from a belt buckle.
threeStarDescription: Say which end points north, and do not trust the needle while the metal is still beside it.

title: Fold a valley crease and leave it
description: Fold one edge to another so the crease bends toward you, and leave the fold in place.
oneStarDescription: Fold one edge of a square to the opposite edge.
twoStarDescription: Flatten the crease so the fold stays where you put it.
threeStarDescription: Point to the crease and say it is a valley fold, bent toward you.

title: Fold one pleat from a valley and a mountain
description: Put one valley crease beside one mountain crease so the paper steps.
oneStarDescription: Pre-crease one valley and one mountain next to each other, then unfold.
twoStarDescription: Fold both creases at once so the paper steps over.
threeStarDescription: Show the pleat from the side so both layers and the step are visible.

title: Fold and unfold to leave a pre-crease
description: Make a valley fold, then open the paper so only the crease remains.
oneStarDescription: Fold one edge of the square to the opposite edge and crease it.
twoStarDescription: Open the paper until it lies flat.
threeStarDescription: Show the crease that remains, and say you are not using it yet.

title: Make a mountain fold by turning the paper over
description: Turn the paper over, make a valley fold, and turn it back so the crease bends away from you.
oneStarDescription: Turn the sheet over so the side you were looking at faces down.
twoStarDescription: Fold the edge that matches the mountain line, as a valley fold, and crease it.
threeStarDescription: Turn the sheet back. The crease now bends away from you.

title: Wash your hands on the surfaces that get missed
description: Wet, soap, and rub the backs, the gaps, the thumbs, and the fingertips, then rinse, dry, and turn the tap off with the towel.
oneStarDescription: Take off rings if you can, wet both hands, and add enough soap to cover them.
twoStarDescription: Rub the backs, between the fingers, the thumbs, and the fingertips. Keep going for about twenty seconds, the timing the NHS page gives.
threeStarDescription: Rinse, dry your hands, turn the tap off with the towel, and name one reason this wash was due, such as food, the toilet, or an animal.

title: Fill a shape with long and short stitches
description: Cover a small shape with straight stitches of uneven length, then start the next row by splitting those stitches.
oneStarDescription: Lay several straight stitches over one edge of a small shape, and make their lengths differ.
twoStarDescription: Fill the other side of that edge the same way, still changing the length.
threeStarDescription: Bring the needle up through a stitch of the first row, not all at the same point, and lay the next stitch.

title: Fold an omelette while the centre is soft
description: Beat eggs, cook them in foaming butter, pull the set edge so liquid fills the gap, and fold while the centre is still soft.
oneStarDescription: Beat the eggs until the white is mixed through, and heat the butter until it foams and has not browned.
twoStarDescription: Pour the eggs in, tilt the pan so they cover the base, and pull a set edge so liquid egg runs into the gap.
threeStarDescription: When the egg has just set and the centre is still soft, fold it and slide it onto a plate.

title: Say how the buds are arranged and stop
description: On one winter twig, say whether the side buds are opposite, alternate, or spiral, and do not name a species from that alone.
oneStarDescription: Point to buds along the twig, not only the bud at the tip.
twoStarDescription: Say whether they sit in opposite pairs, alternate from side to side, or spiral around the twig.
threeStarDescription: If you have only that arrangement, do not name the tree. A species needs a second clue you can point to.

title: Sew a feather stitch that alternates sides
description: Work a band of loops that sit under one another, offset to the left and then the right.
oneStarDescription: Bring the needle up, take it down to the right, and come up inside the loop so it tightens into a V.
twoStarDescription: Make the next loop on the other side of the line, under the first.
threeStarDescription: Continue a short band in which the loops change side each time.

title: Shade a patch with seed stitches
description: Scatter tiny straight stitches in different directions, and make one area denser than another.
oneStarDescription: Make several straight stitches, each only a millimetre or two long, pointing different ways.
twoStarDescription: Place stitches close together in one part of a small shape.
threeStarDescription: Spread stitches farther apart beside it, and say which patch looks darker.

title: Tell needles from scales
description: On a conifer, say whether the foliage is separate needles or overlapping scales, and remember that larch can be bare in winter.
oneStarDescription: Point to growth that is needles or scales rather than a broad blade.
twoStarDescription: Say whether you see separate needles or flattened scales that overlap.
threeStarDescription: Say that a bare twig is not proof against larch, which drops its needles.

title: Fill a leaf with fishbone stitch
description: Cover a small leaf with diagonal stitches that overlap near the centre, working from the tip down.
oneStarDescription: Bring the needle up at the tip and take it down to make one straight stitch along the middle.
twoStarDescription: Come up at one edge, cross the end of the centre stitch, then do the same from the other edge.
threeStarDescription: Keep alternating edges until the leaf is covered, each stitch overlapping the end of the one before.

title: Fold scrambled eggs off the heat
description: Beat eggs with cream or milk, fold them in a pan until they are softly set, and let the pan finish them off the heat.
oneStarDescription: Beat the eggs with cream or milk and salt until the mix is even, and melt butter without letting it brown.
twoStarDescription: Pour the eggs in, leave them briefly, then lift and fold from the edge toward the middle. Wait and fold again.
threeStarDescription: Take the pan off while some egg is still soft, let the pan finish the cooking, and serve.

title: Couch a laid thread
description: Lay a thread on the fabric and catch it with a finer thread so the thick thread stays on the surface.
oneStarDescription: Bring one or more strands to the surface and lay them together along a short line, without stitching that thread down through the cloth.
twoStarDescription: Bring a finer thread up on one side of the laid strands and take it down on the other side, in a new hole rather than the hole you just left.
threeStarDescription: Repeat those small catches at even gaps along the line, then take both threads to the back and fasten them.

title: Create a 3D-printed object
description: Prepare a simple digital model for additive manufacturing, orient and slice it for a printer, then evaluate the physical result and make a purposeful improvement.
oneStarDescription: Select a small, printer-compatible model, inspect the slicing preview and produce a simple object using the printer instructions.
twoStarDescription: Change one dimension or a basic feature of a model and successfully print the revised version.
threeStarDescription: Design or substantially adapt a small object, state what it should do, test the printed result and document one evidence-based revision.

title: Play backgammon strategically
description: Develop backgammon skill by applying legal moves, weighing risk and probability, and reviewing decisions rather than relying only on luck.
oneStarDescription: Complete a game while making legal moves and correctly applying the basic movement and bearing-off rules.
twoStarDescription: During a game, explain the reason for at least three choices involving safety, blocking or race position.
threeStarDescription: Review a completed game, identify two decisions that changed risk or position and compare an alternative move using the same position.
